title: The clauses, verbatim
summary: The page's one paper moment is the document itself: the 8 clauses verbatim in a reading column on the real grid, each under one hairline with its plain number in the margin in the heading's own face at the light weight, clause 01 (the document's summary) at lede size, the rest in the articles' reading style — calm, readable and still.

notes: Reading surface: the section is ≈2,574px at 1440 and deliberately exceeds the 1400px cap — it is not cropped because the founder is reviewing the clauses verbatim. Grid: number cols 1–2, heading and text cols 3–8 — the articles' column and the articles' reading style (18px/1.6, full ink, text-wrap: pretty, hanging punctuation), so the two templates share one ReadingSpread; it sets a median 73–76 characters a line (64–83), wider than the map's 'about 66ch' exactly as the articles do (narrowing is a shared call, see kitNeeds), hairlines cols 1–8, cols 9–12 left empty as the outer margin of a printed page (no sidenotes: legal text carries no glosses). Clause headings are h2 (the h1 is in the header); each carries a visually hidden ‘0n’ so a screen reader hears the number the eye sees in the margin. Inline links use a quiet underline defined here (the kit's three actions are caps components, unusable inside a sentence) — see kitNeeds. Inline links never break across a line (white-space: nowrap), so their underline stays one stroke.
story: Beat 2 of 3. The text, and nothing else: no drawing, no pull quote, no sidenote. Clause 01 is the short version, so it reads first and largest; the rest follow as a plain numbered document.
